description: Redaction vectors for the reference redactors' default patterns (Agent Capability Standard 1.2.0, section 6.7): grounded_agency/state/redaction.py and packages/acs-core/src/redact.ts. Informative: the Standard defines what a secret is and that it is replaced by the marker [REDACTED]; these vectors pin what the two reference redactors recognise, so they agree. Each vector redacts `input` (a string or a JSON value) with `secret_values` registered: `expect.output` is the redacted value and `expect.pointers` the JSON Pointers (RFC 6901) of the members changed, in document order ("" when the input is a string that changed). A vector with `anchor: true` redacts `input` as an evidence anchor (section 6.5) as an evidence store or a trace keeps it (`Redactor.redact_anchor`, `redactAnchor`): `expect.output` is the anchor kept, and `expect.pointers` are still those of the input read as a JSON value. An anchor that held a secret keeps no digest of what it cites: its `digest` and `metadata.hash` go, and its `metadata` says `digest_omitted: "secret"` (section 6.7: a digest of content that may be no more than a secret could be inverted by guessing). Example tokens in a provider's own format (a Discord bot token, a Stripe live key, a Slack webhook URL) are written with one character as a JSON \u escape, so that the file's raw text matches no pattern that secret scanning acts on (a host's push protection, the providers' revocation of tokens found in public code); a JSON reader decodes the escape, so the vectors test the same text.

vectors.name: bearer_header
vectors.about: An Authorization header's value, after its scheme.

vectors.name: authorization_basic
vectors.about: A Basic Authorization header; the scheme stays.

vectors.name: bearer_in_text
vectors.about: A Bearer token outside a header.
vectors.input: retry with Bearer abcdefgh12345678 if it fails

expect.output: retry with Bearer [REDACTED] if it fails

vectors.name: url_userinfo
vectors.about: The password of a URL's userinfo; the user and host stay.

vectors.name: url_userinfo_scheme_in_a_word
vectors.about: A URL's scheme is a run of scheme characters that holds a letter, wherever the run starts: the password is redacted after `_` too.

vectors.name: query_token
vectors.about: A credential in a query string; the other parameters stay.

vectors.name: password_assignment
vectors.about: An assignment to a name that ends in a credential name.

vectors.name: json_text_token
vectors.about: A credential member in JSON text.

vectors.name: api_key_json_member
vectors.about: A string member whose name is a credential name is redacted whole.

vectors.name: structured_headers
vectors.about: Headers as JSON members: the Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, Cookie and Set-Cookie values are redacted whole, as their text form is; other headers stay.

vectors.name: camel_case_members
vectors.about: A member name that ends in a credential name after any prefix, camelCase included, is redacted whole; a name that only contains one (max_tokens, tokenCount) is not.

vectors.name: secret_member_name
vectors.about: A registered value used as a member name: the name is redacted as text, and the member keeps its value.

vectors.name: credential_shaped_member_name
vectors.about: A credential-shaped member name (a GitHub token) is redacted as text; its value is walked under the new name.

vectors.name: colliding_member_names
vectors.about: Two names that redact to the same text, and one already in the object: each later one gets a number, so that no member is lost.

vectors.name: pem_private_key
vectors.about: A PEM private key's body.
vectors.input:
-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----
MIIEowIBAAKCAQEA
-----END RSA PRIVATE KEY-----

expect.output: -----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----[REDACTED]-----END RSA PRIVATE KEY-----

vectors.name: aws_access_key_id
vectors.about: An AWS access key id.

vectors.name: github_token
vectors.about: A GitHub token.

vectors.name: github_token_alone
vectors.about: A GitHub token in prose.

vectors.name: slack_token
vectors.about: A Slack token.

vectors.name: sk_key
vectors.about: An sk- key in prose.

vectors.name: jwt
vectors.about: A JWT.

vectors.name: jwt_after_dash
vectors.about: A JWT starts at a word boundary: after `-` in a run of base64url characters, not after a letter.

vectors.name: pem_header_without_end
vectors.about: A PEM header with no end after it: the rest of the text is replaced, since an excerpt of a key keeps its body (security round 4, batch 5: nothing was replaced, and a key cut before its end line was kept whole).

vectors.name: registered_value
vectors.about: A value the host registered, wherever it occurs.

vectors.name: registered_value_short_ignored
vectors.about: A registered value shorter than four characters is ignored.

vectors.name: no_false_positive_tokens_py
vectors.about: A file name that holds a credential name is not an assignment.

vectors.name: short_assignment_kept
vectors.about: An assignment of fewer than four characters is kept.

vectors.name: marker_kept
vectors.about: A value already redacted stays as it is, and is not reported again.

vectors.name: nested_json_pointers
vectors.about: Nested members are redacted and their pointers returned in document order, escaped as RFC 6901 says.

vectors.name: no_secret_json
vectors.about: A value without a secret is unchanged.

vectors.name: astral_value_counts_code_points
vectors.about: A credential value is counted in characters (code points): three, one of them outside the BMP, is too short.

vectors.name: non_ascii_letters_do_not_fold
vectors.about: Names match case-insensitively in ASCII only: a long s is not an s.

vectors.name: unicode_space_is_not_whitespace
vectors.about: Only ASCII whitespace separates a name from its value; another space is part of the value.

vectors.name: prefixed_assignment
vectors.about: An assignment to a longer name that ends in a credential name with no separator (PGPASSWORD): the refusal rule recognises it, so redaction does too.

vectors.name: secret_member_list
vectors.about: A secret member whose value is a list: each string in it is redacted.

vectors.name: secret_member_object
vectors.about: A secret member whose value is an object: each string in it is redacted, its names kept.

vectors.name: secret_member_number
vectors.about: A secret member whose value is a number (a PIN) is redacted whole.

vectors.name: structured_header_list
vectors.about: A header given as a list of values.

vectors.name: secret_member_flags_kept
vectors.about: Booleans and null in a secret member hold no secret and are kept, as is a string shorter than four characters.

vectors.name: har_header_pairs
vectors.about: Headers as name/value pairs (a HAR's request.headers): the value of a pair whose name is a secret member's is redacted whole; other headers stay.

vectors.name: pair_name_members
vectors.about: A pair's name may be its key or header member, in any case (Postman, AWS tags); its value member is redacted.

vectors.name: header_tuples
vectors.about: Headers as [name, value] tuples (fetch's entries, Python's http.client): the second element of a two-element array whose first is a secret member's name is redacted; other tuples stay.

vectors.name: har_cookies
vectors.about: A HAR's cookies member is a secret member: every string in it is redacted, a cookie's name included; its member names stay.

vectors.name: pair_in_text
vectors.about: A name/value pair in JSON or code text: the value after a secret member's name and a value label is redacted, after its scheme.

vectors.name: tuple_in_text
vectors.about: A [name, value] tuple in code text: the value after an opening bracket and a secret member's name is redacted.

vectors.name: anchor_excerpt_drops_digest
vectors.about: An anchor whose excerpt quotes a secret loses the digest of what it cites: the excerpt left around the marker would let a guess of the password be checked against the digest.

vectors.name: anchor_registered_secret_alone
vectors.about: A host's registered secret quoted whole: the digest, of the secret alone, goes with it.

vectors.name: anchor_ref_drops_metadata_hash
vectors.about: A secret in the ref: a content hash kept in the metadata goes too, and the other metadata stays.

vectors.name: anchor_metadata_secret_drops_digest
vectors.about: A secret in the metadata only: the anchor keeps no digest either.

vectors.name: anchor_secret_without_digest
vectors.about: An anchor with a secret and no digest: redacted, and nothing is said of a digest it never had.

vectors.name: anchor_without_secret_keeps_digest
vectors.about: An anchor with no secret keeps its digest.

vectors.name: url_userinfo_empty_user
vectors.about: The password of a URL's userinfo whose user's name is empty (Redis's form).

vectors.name: escaped_json_text
vectors.about: An assignment in JSON text inside a JSON string or a shell's double quotes: its quotes escaped.

vectors.name: escaped_json_text_twice
vectors.about: JSON text escaped twice; the escapes around the marker stay.

vectors.name: escaped_authorization_and_pair
vectors.about: An Authorization header and a header pair in escaped JSON text.

vectors.name: user_option
vectors.about: A command's user option: the password after the user's name (curl -u, --user, -U, --proxy-user).
vectors.input: curl -u admin:S3cr3tP4ss https://a.example.com; curl --user=ops:hunter22 -U proxy:Pr0xyPass99 https://b.example.com

expect.output: curl -u admin:[REDACTED] https://a.example.com; curl --user=ops:[REDACTED] -U proxy:[REDACTED] https://b.example.com

vectors.name: user_option_list_item
vectors.about: A user option and its value as items of a list, as an exception's text quotes a command.

vectors.name: credential_option
vectors.about: A command's option named for a credential, its value after blanks.

vectors.name: credential_option_before_an_option
vectors.about: An option named for a credential followed by another option: no value.

vectors.name: user_option_without_password
vectors.about: Options that take no user:password pair are kept.
vectors.input: git push -u origin main && sort -u names.txt

expect.output: git push -u origin main && sort -u names.txt

vectors.name: secret_key_and_passphrase
vectors.about: SECRET_KEY, secret_key and passphrase are credential names.

vectors.name: secret_key_members
vectors.about: Members named secret_key and passphrase are secret members.

vectors.name: registered_value_encoded
vectors.about: A registered value is replaced in the forms text carries it in: percent-encoded (upper- or lower-case hex) and JSON-escaped.

vectors.name: registered_value_non_ascii
vectors.about: A registered value with non-ASCII characters, escaped as \u in JSON text and percent-encoded as UTF-8.

vectors.name: quoted_value_with_whitespace
vectors.about: A quoted value after a credential name is read to its closing quote on its line, whitespace and all, its quotes escaped or not: a passphrase is replaced whole, not its first word.
vectors.input: cfg {"passphrase": "correct horse battery staple"} py {'password': 'it is a secret'} env DB_PASSWORD="a,b;c&d e" body={\"password\": \"correct horse\"}

vectors.name: quoted_pair_and_tuple_values
vectors.about: A header or credential given as a pair or tuple in text: its quoted value is read to its closing quote, so a Cookie header's later cookies are replaced too.

vectors.name: quoted_option_values
vectors.about: A credential option's quoted value and a quoted user option's password are read to the closing quote, as text and as a list's items.
vectors.input: mysql --password "correct horse battery" -h db; curl -u 'admin:correct horse' https://x; ['--api-key', 'abc def ghi']

vectors.name: quoted_value_controls
vectors.about: A quoted value shorter than four characters is not read past its closing quote; a value with no closing quote on its line is read as an unquoted one, to a blank; a quoted value does not continue onto the next line.
vectors.input:
password: "x" and then "something else"
password: "unterminated value here
password: "abc
def ghi"

expect.output:
password: "x" and then "something else"
password: "[REDACTED] value here
password: "abc
def ghi"

vectors.name: registered_value_as_number
vectors.about: A registered value given as a JSON number (a card number, a PIN): a number whose JSON text holds one is replaced whole, as the redaction of the JSON text would replace it, in a list too; other numbers and booleans stay.

vectors.name: anchor_registered_number_drops_digest
vectors.about: An anchor whose metadata holds a registered PIN as a number: the number is replaced and the digest goes, as for a string.

vectors.name: authorization_other_schemes
vectors.about: An Authorization or Proxy-Authorization header whose scheme is not one of bearer, basic, token, digest and negotiate (ApiKey, SSWS, Bot, Splunk, GenieKey, Key): the scheme and the credential after it are replaced, in a header line, a quoted header line, a JSON member and code text; after one of the five, the scheme stays in view.
vectors.input:
curl -H "Authorization: ApiKey VnVhQ2ZHY0JDZGJrUXctN1A6dWkybGp0YjU0" https://es.example.com
Authorization: SSWS 00QCjAl4MlV-WPXM8M1vdfSD0gvwxVNHEs7QjL3Vgs
Proxy-Authorization: Bot MTk4NjIyNDgzNDcxOTI1MjQ4.Cl2FMQ.ZnCjm1XVW7vRze4b7Cq4se7kKWs
{"Authorization": "Splunk 8a1b2c3d-4e5f-6789-abcd-ef0123456789"}
{'Authorization': 'GenieKey 0a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f9'}
authorization=Key 9f8e7d6c5b4a39281706abcd
Authorization: Bearer abcdefgh12345678

expect.output:
curl -H "Authorization: [REDACTED]" https://es.example.com
Authorization: [REDACTED]
Proxy-Authorization: [REDACTED]
{"Authorization": "[REDACTED]"}
{'Authorization': '[REDACTED]'}
authorization=[REDACTED]
Authorization: Bearer [REDACTED]

vectors.name: authorization_quoted_multi_param
vectors.about: A header line quoted whole (curl -H) with a scheme of several parameters: read to its closing quote, every parameter included.

vectors.name: authorization_without_scheme_and_a_word
vectors.about: A credential with no scheme, then a word on its line: both are replaced, since the layer cannot tell a scheme from a credential.

vectors.name: authorization_other_scheme_pair_and_tuple
vectors.about: A header given as a name/value pair or a tuple in text, with a scheme of its own: the value is replaced whole.

vectors.name: pgp_private_key_block
vectors.about: An OpenPGP private key block (RFC 4880 armor, `PRIVATE KEY BLOCK`): its armor headers and body.
vectors.input:
-----BEGIN PGP PRIVATE KEY BLOCK-----
Version: GnuPG v2

lQOYBGVhY2sBCADKx3mYq7vT2bN9cW4pLk8sR1fJ0dE6aH3gU5iO2yM7nB4
=AbCd
-----END PGP PRIVATE KEY BLOCK-----

expect.output: -----BEGIN PGP PRIVATE KEY BLOCK-----[REDACTED]-----END PGP PRIVATE KEY BLOCK-----

vectors.name: pem_body_without_end
vectors.about: A PEM header with a body and no end line (an excerpt, `head -n 2 key.pem`, a truncated log line): the rest of the text is replaced, so no part of the key is kept.
vectors.input:
cannot import key: -----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----
MIIEowIBAAKCAQEAu1SU1LfVLPHCozMxH2Mo4lgOEePzNm0tRgeLezV6ffAt0gunVTLw

expect.output: cannot import key: -----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----[REDACTED]

vectors.name: pgp_block_without_end
vectors.about: An OpenPGP private key block with no end line: the rest of the text is replaced.

vectors.name: pem_header_alone
vectors.about: A private key's opening line with nothing after it holds no body: nothing is replaced (the refusal rule still recognises it).

vectors.name: cookie_header_line
vectors.about: A Cookie header line's value, from its first character to the end of its line: every cookie of it.

vectors.name: set_cookie_header_line
vectors.about: A Set-Cookie header line's value, its attributes with it.

vectors.name: cookie_member_in_text
vectors.about: A Cookie header as a member in JSON or code text (a headers dictionary an exception quotes), read to its closing quote.

vectors.name: cookie_header_quoted_whole
vectors.about: A Cookie header line quoted whole, as a command or its list of arguments quotes it, read to its closing quote.
vectors.input: Command '['curl', '-fsS', '-H', 'Cookie: sessionid=8f3k2l9d0s7a6q5w4e3r2t1yQ', 'https://app.example/api']' returned non-zero exit status 22.

vectors.name: curl_cookie_option
vectors.about: curl's cookie option given a cookie string (a name and `=`), quoted or not, or as a list's next item; a cookie file's name and another program's `-b` stay.
vectors.input: curl -b 'sessionid=8f3k2l9d0s7a6q5w4e3r2t1yQ' https://x; curl --cookie sid=8f3k2l9d0s7a6q5w4e3r2t1yQ https://x; ['-b', 'sid=8f3k2l9d0s7a6q5w4e3r2t1yQ']; curl -b cookies.txt https://x; git checkout -b feature-2024

expect.output: curl -b '[REDACTED]' https://x; curl --cookie [REDACTED] https://x; ['-b', '[REDACTED]']; curl -b cookies.txt https://x; git checkout -b feature-2024

vectors.name: url_userinfo_escaped_slashes
vectors.about: The password of a URL's userinfo whose slashes are escaped, as PHP's json_encode writes a URL.

vectors.name: quote_json_escapes
vectors.about: Quotes written as JSON escapes of their code points (`\u0022`), as .NET's encoder writes JSON text inside a JSON string: an assignment's value, an Authorization header's credential and a header pair's value.

vectors.name: equals_json_escape
vectors.about: An assignment whose `=` is its JSON escape (`\u003d`), as Gson writes it.

vectors.name: token_after_quote_escape
vectors.about: A token right after a quote's JSON escape: the escape's last character is a digit, so a word boundary alone would not start the token there.

vectors.name: registered_value_html_safe
vectors.about: A registered value as encoders that keep JSON safe inside HTML write it: Go's encoding/json (`&`, `<`, `>`), Gson (also `=` and `'`), and .NET's System.Text.Json (also `'`, `+`, upper-case hex).

vectors.name: netrc_password
vectors.about: A .netrc entry's password.
vectors.input: cannot parse ~/.netrc line: 'machine api.example.com login bot password 8f3k2l9d0s7a6q5w4e3r2t1yQ'

expect.output: cannot parse ~/.netrc line: 'machine api.example.com login bot password [REDACTED]'
